title: DynaCI: Generating GitHub Actions Workflows via Dynamic Analysis
title_zh: DynaCI：通过动态分析生成GitHub Actions工作流

paragraphs.en: Continuous Integration (CI) is an essential practice that automatically validates code changes through builds and tests. However, configuring CI workflows remains challenging, as modern software often features complex architectures, numerous dependencies, and support for diverse execution environments. Most CI platforms also require workflows to be written in their particular domain-specific languages. As a result, CI workflows are often error-prone and hard to maintain, especially for those unfamiliar with CI semantics. Prior work on automated CI workflow generation require developers to create specifications that describe their intended workflows using natural language, partial workflows, etc. However, in practice, developers may struggle to articulate requirements and may be unaware of available CI features.
paragraphs.zh: 持续集成（CI）是一项重要的实践，它通过构建和测试自动验证代码变更。 然而，配置 CI 工作流仍然具有挑战性，因为现代软件往往具有复杂的架构、大量的依赖项，并且需要支持多样的执行环境。 大多数 CI 平台还要求使用其特定的领域专用语言来编写工作流。 因此，CI 工作流往往容易出错且难以维护，对于不熟悉 CI 语义的人来说尤其如此。 先前关于自动化 CI 工作流生成的工作要求开发者创建规范，使用自然语言、部分工作流等来描述其预期的工作流。 然而，在实践中，开发者可能难以清楚地表达需求，并且可能不了解可用的 CI 特性。

paragraphs.en: To address these limitations, we propose DynaCI , a novel approach that uses runtime information from developers’ local environments to generate CI workflows. DynaCI (i) traces the developers’ local environment to collect runtime information, (ii) constructs an initial workflow by applying runtime-informed heuristics, and (iii) iteratively refines the workflow via LLM-based Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG). We evaluate DynaCI on 50 popular Python projects that use GitHub Actions, a popular CI platform, and compare it against the state-of-the-art CI workflow generation approaches: GH-WCOM and LLM4GW . DynaCI outperforms these existing approaches by more than 21.13% in BLEU score and 20.96% in F1 score on average. It also generates workflows without missing functionality in 56% of cases, while requiring fewer manual modifications to repair such exceptions. These results demonstrate that leveraging runtime information substantially improves LLM-based CI workflow generation, and offer a promising direction for broader DevOps configuration automation.

paragraphs.en: Continuous Integration (CI) is a popular software engineering practice that automates the code integration process in software repositories [ 1 ] . Prior work shows that CI enables faster pull request acceptance and frequent releases [ 2 ] , increases the number of change merges [ 3 ] , and boosts developer productivity, efficiency, and confidence [ 4 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 持续集成（CI）是一种流行的软件工程实践，用于自动化软件仓库中的代码集成过程 [ 1 ] 。 已有研究表明，CI 能够加快拉取请求的接受速度并实现更频繁的发布 [ 2 ] ，增加变更合并的数量 [ 3 ] ，并提升开发者的生产率、效率和信心 [ 4 ] 。

sents.en: Continuous Integration (CI) is a popular software engineering practice that automates the code integration process in software repositories [ 1 ] .

sents.en: Prior work shows that CI enables faster pull request acceptance and frequent releases [ 2 ] , increases the number of change merges [ 3 ] , and boosts developer productivity, efficiency, and confidence [ 4 ] .
sents.zh: 已有研究表明，CI 能够加快拉取请求的接受速度并实现更频繁的发布 [ 2 ] ，增加变更合并的数量 [ 3 ] ，并提升开发者的生产率、效率和信心 [ 4 ] 。

paragraphs.en: While there are many CI platforms [ 5 , 6 , 7 ] , GitHub Actions (GHA) remains the most widely used [ 2 , 8 ] , with at least 71.8% of popular GitHub repositories containing a workflow since 2023 [ 9 , 10 ] . Since December 2025, developers can define a GHA workflow in a YAML using 84 different components, such as event triggers, jobs, steps, actions, runners, matrices, containers, secrets, and conditional rules [ 11 ] . With such a capacity for extensive customization, configuring CI workflows is inherently challenging for developers. Saroar et al. [ 12 ] surveyed 90 developers and found that 60.87% often encounter difficulties writing workflows. Among these, the most common challenges were related to confusing and error-prone syntax. Zhang et al. [ 13 ] studied 6,590 Stack Overflow questions and 315 GitHub issues, and found that workflow configuration issues were discussed more than those related to dependencies, security, integration, deployment, etc. Again, the most common problem among these issues was workflows’ ”nightmare” syntax [ 13 ] . Valenzuela-Toledo et al. [ 14 ] has argued that this trend is due, in part, to inadequate tooling support for writing GHA workflows.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管存在许多 CI 平台 [ 5 , 6 , 7 ] ，GitHub Actions（GHA）仍然是使用最广泛的平台 [ 2 , 8 ] ，自 2023 年以来，至少有 71.8% 的热门 GitHub 仓库包含工作流 [ 9 , 10 ] 。 自 2025 年 12 月起，开发者可以在 YAML 中使用 84 种不同的组件来定义 GHA 工作流，例如事件触发器、作业、步骤、动作、运行器、矩阵、容器、密钥和条件规则 [ 11 ] 。 由于具备如此广泛的定制能力，配置 CI 工作流对开发者来说本身就具有挑战性。Saroar 等人 [ 12 ] 调查了 90 名开发者，发现 60.87% 的开发者经常在编写工作流时遇到困难。 其中，最常见的挑战与令人困惑且容易出错的语法有关。Zhang 等人 [ 13 ] 研究了 6,590 个 Stack Overflow 问题和 315 个 GitHub issue，发现工作流配置问题被讨论的次数多于与依赖、安全、集成、部署等相关的问题。 同样，这些问题中最常见的是工作流的“噩梦”般语法 [ 13 ] 。Valenzuela-Toledo 等人 [ 14 ] 认为这种趋势的部分原因是编写 GHA 工作流的工具支持不足。

paragraphs.en: Previous works have attempted to provide this tooling support. For example, Mastropaolo et al. [ 15 ] propose GH-WCOM , a transformer-based approach that provides code completion suggestions for GHA workflows. Zhang et al. [ 16 ] propose LLM4GW , a set of prompting techniques that optimize the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) on GHA workflow generation, syntactic error identification, code injection vulnerability detection, syntactic error fixing, and code injection vulnerability repair. However, despite their intended benefits, these tools may fall short in practice, as they still require inputs that demand substantial domain knowledge of GHA to produce acceptable configurations. GH-WCOM [ 15 ] , for example, still requires a developer to write the majority of their workflows beforehand so that it can fill in any gaps. LLM4GW [ 16 ] accepts natural language instructions instead, but developers must provide detailed workflow-, job-, and step-level specifications for functional correctness.

paragraphs.en: To address these concerns, we propose DynaCI , the first tool, to the best of our knowledge, that combines runtime analysis with LLMs to synthesize GHA workflows. Our intuition is that a developer’s local environment can serve as a starting point for extracting the information required for generating CI workflows. As the developer runs test suites in their local environment, DynaCI collects runtime traces and extracts information about the executed commands, dependencies, and execution order. It then applies heuristics to select candidate GHA settings (i.e., components), assembles an initial workflow, and iteratively refines it using LLM-based Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) [ 17 , 18 ] . We evaluate DynaCI against GH-WCOM and LLM4GW , the state-of-the-art in GHA workflow synthesis tools, on 50 popular Python projects to answer the following research questions:
paragraphs.zh: 为了解决这些问题，我们提出了 DynaCI，据我们所知，这是首个将运行时分析与 LLM 相结合来合成 GHA 工作流的工具。 我们的直觉是，开发者的本地环境可以作为起点，用于提取生成 CI 工作流所需的信息。 当开发者在本地环境中运行测试套件时，DynaCI 会收集运行时轨迹，并提取有关所执行命令、依赖项和执行顺序的信息。 然后，它应用启发式方法来选择候选的 GHA 设置（即组件），组装出初始工作流，并使用基于 LLM 的检索增强生成（RAG）[17, 18] 对其进行迭代式优化。 我们在 50 个热门 Python 项目上，将 DynaCI 与当前最先进的 GHA 工作流合成工具 GH-WCOM 和 LLM4GW 进行对比评估，以回答以下研究问题：

paragraphs.en: 𝐑𝐐 𝟏 \mathbf{RQ_{1}} How effective is DynaCI at generating CI workflows? To assess whether DynaCI outperforms the state-of-the-art, we compare the tools’ workflows against their targets across several popular workflow similarity metrics. We found that DynaCI has a BLEU score [ 19 ] of 52.81% and a F1 score of 62.06%, outperforming the state-of-the-art by more than 21.13% and 20.96%, respectively.

paragraphs.en: GHA workflows automate the building, testing, and deployment activities for a GitHub repository and are configured through YAML files. Figure 1 (A) shows an example configuration file that illustrates the main components of a GHA workflow. A workflow is triggered in response to an event , which executes its jobs. A job is a sequence of steps that run on a shared machine to accomplish a set of tasks. It can initialize environmental variables , set a maximum number of minutes to run , use a matrix that repeats the job with different configurations , and stop queued configurations if any fails . A step is a group of shell commands that accomplish a single task, such as or , which performs software quality assurance. An action is a reusable step whose contents are hosted in an external repository. For example, checks out a repository into the runner so that the workflow can access it, sets up a particular Python version in the execution environment, and does the same with uv , a popular Python package manager. These, alongside services, containers, and 84 additional settings [ 20 ] , make workflows difficult to write without supporting tools [ 12 , 13 , 14 ] .

paragraphs.en: Figure 1 (B) presents four scenarios in which a developer tries to create a workflow. In scenario , which is the most common, the developer attempts to write the entire workflow without using tools. This requires them to (i) articulate their needs and (ii) leverage substantial domain knowledge about GHA. Since most developers do not meet either condition [ 12 ] , scenario introduces GH-WCOM [ 15 ] , a tool that auto-completes any gaps that a developer leaves behind in a GHA workflow file. While this mitigates the knowledge requirement, the developer must still be familiar enough with GHA to write a partial workflow. For those who are not familiar with writing GHA configuration files, LLM4GW [ 16 ] can be used, as shown in scenario , where the developer writes natural language instructions instead of a (partial) workflow. However, the instructions required for this scenario can still be complex and require substantial domain knowledge about GHA, such that developers may expend effort comparable to that required in the first scenario. To fill the gaps in the previous scenarios, we introduce DynaCI —scenario in Figure 1 (B). DynaCI traces the developer’s local environment during execution and uses the runtime information to generate and refine the workflow. Besides performing their regular development and testing tasks and attaching DynaCI to their environment, the developer is not required to produce additional inputs, such as workflow components (e.g., and ) or natural language instructions (e.g., ).

paragraphs.en: Software testing is crucial for improving code quality and reliability [ 21 ] . Before contributing code changes to shared repositories, developers typically validate their changes in local development environments, where test executions have access to project-specific resources such as test files, software packages, and environment variables [ 22 ] . To perform these validation activities, developers execute build and test commands that exercise the project’s functionality. This fundamental software engineering practice helps detect faults before code changes are pushed to shared repositories, avoiding unnecessary CI wait times [ 23 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 软件测试对于提高代码质量和可靠性至关重要 [ 21 ] 。 在向共享仓库提交代码变更之前，开发者通常会在本地开发环境中验证他们的变更，在这些环境中，测试执行可以访问项目特定的资源，例如测试文件、软件包和环境变量 [ 22 ] 。 为了执行这些验证活动，开发者会运行构建和测试命令来检验项目的功能。 这项基本的软件工程实践有助于在代码变更被推送到共享仓库之前检测缺陷，从而避免不必要的持续集成等待时间 [ 23 ] 。

paragraphs.en: Once a developer identifies their project’s building and testing commands (via its documentation and configurations), they can run those commands in their local environment. To start generating a CI workflow, the developer provides their set of commands, as an input file, to DynaCI , which will execute them in the same environment twice to trace their runtime information. In the first execution ( Section III-B1 ), it captures runtime traces, such as durations of commands, file accesses in system calls, and dependency installations in package managers, using strace [ 24 ] . In the second execution ( Section III-B2 ), DynaCI captures environment variable accesses using ltrace [ 25 ] . This separation is necessary since multiple ptrace tools, such as strace and ltrace , cannot attach to the same process at the same time [ 26 ] . Below, we discuss these two execution runs in detail.

paragraphs.en: Command probe. Developers typically execute a sequence of commands to prepare, build, test, and validate a project in their local environment. While these commands collectively accomplish multiple tasks, their boundaries are not explicitly demarcated. This poses a challenge when synthesizing CI workflows, where commands must be organized into semantically meaningful workflow steps [ 27 , 28 ] . To address this problem, DynaCI introduces a Command probe that analyzes developer command sequences and partitions them into executable units that can later be mapped to workflow steps. Each unit is a command or expression node that is defined at the top-level of a command sequence’s parse tree [ 29 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 命令探针。 开发人员通常会在本地环境中执行一系列命令来准备、构建、测试和验证项目。 虽然这些命令共同完成了多项任务，但它们之间的边界并没有被明确划分。 这在合成 CI 工作流时带来了挑战，因为命令必须被组织成语义上有意义的工作流步骤 [ 27 , 28 ] 。 为了解决这个问题，DynaCI 引入了命令探针，它分析开发人员的命令序列，并将其划分为可执行单元，这些单元之后可以被映射到工作流步骤。 每个单元是一个命令节点或表达式节点，定义在命令序列解析树的顶层 [ 29 ] 。

paragraphs.en: Python environ probe. This probe captures environment variable accesses by a language-specific runtime interface. Many runtimes, such as the Python interpreter and the Java Virtual Machine, provide an abstraction over the underlying OS environment. The probe instruments this abstraction to record environment variables that are accessed during execution. For Python, we implement the probe using a site-specific customization script that leverages the environ interface in the os module to capture environment variables during interpreter initialization [ 34 ] . This approach can be readily extended to other languages; for example, in Java, a similar probe can be implemented using agent-based instrumentation via java.lang.instrument [ 35 ] .
paragraphs.zh: Python 环境探针。 该探针通过特定语言的运行时接口捕获环境变量的访问。 许多运行时（例如 Python 解释器和 Java 虚拟机）都对底层操作系统环境提供了抽象。 该探针对这一抽象进行插桩，以记录执行期间被访问的环境变量。 对于 Python，我们使用一个站点定制的初始化脚本实现该探针，该脚本利用 os 模块中的 environ 接口在解释器初始化期间捕获环境变量 [ 34 ] 。 这种方法可以很容易地扩展到其他语言；例如在 Java 中，可以通过 java.lang.instrument 基于智能体的插桩实现类似的探针 [ 35 ] 。

paragraphs.en: In this phase, DynaCI applies heuristics to runtime information collected from the developer’s local environment (e.g., commands, dependencies, and environment variables) to construct an initial workflow that will be refined later.
paragraphs.zh: 在此阶段，DynaCI 应用启发式方法处理从开发者本地环境中收集的运行时信息（例如命令、依赖项和环境变量），以构建一个初始工作流，后续将对其进行细化。

paragraphs.en: As of December 2025, GHA supports 84 workflow components, each representing a configurable element of a workflow [ 20 ] . However, some components are CI-specific and do not correspond to configurations that exist in a developer’s local environment. Since DynaCI aims to generate workflows from local environments, it avoids using components that do not have local counterparts unless their inclusion is required to run the workflow. We grouped the 84 workflow components into eight categories using official GHA documentation [ 20 ] . For three of the most important categories, below, we discuss our inclusion and exclusion criteria for identifying candidate workflow components.
paragraphs.zh: 截至 2025 年 12 月，GHA 支持 84 种工作流组件，每一种都代表工作流中一个可配置的元素 [ 20 ] 。 然而，其中一些组件是持续集成（CI）专用的，与开发者本地环境中存在的配置并不对应。 由于 DynaCI 旨在从本地环境生成工作流，因此它会避免使用没有本地对应物的组件，除非必须包含它们才能运行工作流。 我们依据 GHA 官方文档 [ 20 ] ，将这 84 种工作流组件归为八个类别。 对于下文中最重要的三个类别，我们讨论了用于确定候选工作流组件的纳入与排除标准。

paragraphs.en: Environment (27/84) , i.e., the components that define key-value pairs that can be accessed by other workflow components: These pairs are either provided to the workflow as secrets, i.e., confidential settings that are not available to our research or the general public (21), or as hard-coded values in the workflow’s file (6). The latter typically specify environment variables required by the workflow, a job, or an individual step. Since GitHub-provided inputs are not available during local execution, DynaCI can only add environment variables that are observable in a local execution environment.
paragraphs.zh: 环境变量（27/84），即定义可被其他工作流组件访问的键值对的组件：这些键值对要么作为机密提供给工作流，即我们的研究或公众无法获取的机密配置（21），要么作为硬编码的值写在工作流文件中（6）。 后者通常指定工作流、某个作业或单个步骤所需的环境变量。 由于 GitHub 提供的输入在本地执行时不可用，DynaCI 只能添加在本地执行环境中可观察到的环境变量。

paragraphs.en: Execution (10/84) , i.e., the components that interact with the OS or shell context: These components either configure the OS and shell environment (7) or execute commands within these environments (3). We exclude the former components from DynaCI workflows since their usage in real-world workflows is exceedingly rare. paragraphs.en: Using the runtime information extracted in Section III-B , DynaCI identifies the candidate components discussed in Section III-C1 . It then applies the following non-parametric heuristics ---rule-based decisions derived directly from the observed runtime behavior---to generate a preliminary workflow file. These heuristics rely solely on the runtime information collected from the developer’s environment and do not depend on tunable parameters. 2 2 2 Note that some heuristics require parameters whose values must be derived empirically; these parametric heuristics are described in Section III-C3 .
paragraphs.zh: 利用第 III-B 节中提取的运行时信息，DynaCI 识别出第 III-C1 节所讨论的候选组件。 随后，它应用以下非参数化启发式规则——直接从观察到的运行时行为中得出的基于规则的决策——来生成初步的工作流文件。 这些启发式规则仅依赖于从开发者环境中收集的运行时信息，而不依赖可调参数。2 2 2 请注意，某些启发式规则需要参数，其取值必须通过经验推导得出；这些参数化启发式规则将在第 III-C3 节中描述。

paragraphs.en: For each job, set the environment variables extracted from the runtime traces: In GHA, jobs. < < id > > .env defines environment variables accessible to all steps in a job. Based on runtime information, DynaCI initializes this component with variables accessed in the developer’s local environment.
paragraphs.zh: 对于每个任务（job），设置从运行时追踪中提取的环境变量：在 GHA 中，jobs.<<id>>.env 定义了任务中所有步骤都可访问的环境变量。 基于运行时信息，DynaCI 使用开发者本地环境中访问过的变量来初始化该组件。

paragraphs.en: For each job, set the configuration matrix using the programming language version and OS name extracted from runtime traces: In GHA, jobs. < < id > > .strategy.matrix defines a matrix of configurations under which a job runs. Most matrices cover a range of programming language versions, such as Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, and specify the machines on which the workflow runs, such as GitHub-hosted Ubuntu, Windows, and MacOS runners. DynaCI defines the matrix in each job using the OS and Python version observed in runtime traces. However, DynaCI currently relies on Linux-specific tools (e.g., strace , ltrace ) to capture runtime information, so it only generates workflows for the GHA Ubuntu runner, accounting for 64.6% of workflow jobs in GHA in general [ 36 ] .

paragraphs.en: For each job, derive workflow steps from runtime information: In GHA, the sequence of tasks that a job performs is specified by jobs. < < id > > .steps[*] . According to runtime information, DynaCI adds a step to each job that installs the apt and pip packages that are missing in the developer’s local dependency configuration file (e.g., requirements.txt ). DynaCI also groups the developer’s commands into separate steps. First, commands (from the Command probe) are partitioned into candidate step groups, preserving order and ensuring each step contains at least one command. Second, DynaCI determines the total size, in LoC, and duration of each group using the runtime information extracted from the Command probe and the Duration probe. Third, it uses Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM) [ 37 , 38 ] to find the step group that minimizes the spread of command durations across its steps while also maximizing the total number of steps. This is based on our intuition that there are primary commands, which perform the main activities and thus run longer (e.g., pytest ), that are surrounded by shorter secondary commands, which provide support (e.g., echo ).

paragraphs.en: Some of GHA components require parameter information that cannot be extracted from runtime traces, and are CI- or project-specific (e.g., setting timeout and concurrency parameters). In our study, we classify such parameters into two categories: threshold parameters and multiplier parameters. A threshold parameter specifies the minimum execution duration a job must have before a workflow component is included (e.g., enabling concurrency and timeout settings). This allows DynaCI to add such GHA components into a workflow only for potential longer-running jobs, where such components are more useful. A multiplier parameter determines the numeric value of a workflow component by scaling the observed job duration (e.g., setting timeout limits once the timeout component is included). This allows DynaCI to determine the numerical value for setting certain components that are related to a job’s runtime duration, i.e., the sum of the durations of corresponding commands executed in the developer’s local environment, as reported by the Duration probe.
paragraphs.zh: GHA 的部分组件需要一些无法从运行时追踪中提取、且与 CI 或具体项目相关的参数信息（例如设置超时和并发参数）。 在我们的研究中，我们将这类参数分为两类：阈值参数和乘数参数。 阈值参数用于指定工作流组件被纳入之前，一个作业必须达到的最短执行时长（例如启用并发和超时设置）。 这使得 DynaCI 只为可能运行时间较长的作业在工作流中加入此类 GHA 组件，因为这类组件在此类作业中更有用。 乘数参数通过缩放观测到的作业时长来确定工作流组件的数值（例如在纳入超时组件后设置超时上限）。 这使得 DynaCI 能够为某些与作业运行时长相关的组件确定设置数值，即由 Duration 探针所报告的、在开发者本地环境中执行的相应命令的时长之和。

paragraphs.en: We derived these parameters from Cardoen et al.’s dataset of 2,595,399 GHA workflows [ 10 ] . We first filtered this dataset by removing invalid workflows, old versions of valid workflows, and workflows that are unrelated to Python-based CI. We consider a workflow to be valid if it conforms to a GHA workflow schema [ 42 ] , and a workflow is Python-based if its repository’s most popular language is Python according to the GitHub REST API [ 43 ] . Doing so resulted in 15,285 workflows, which we call the CI Workflow Dataset . Setting aside 50 workflows with the highest star counts for our Evaluation Dataset ( Section IV ), we used the GitHub REST API to extract the last successful job runs, if any, from the remaining 15,235 workflows. This left us with 7,157 job runs, which we refer to as the Heuristic-Tuning Dataset . For the workflow components below, we extracted the durations of job runs that use them, removed their outliers, and treated their averages as default threshold and multiplier values. Below, we list these parameter values and their associated heuristics, which DynaCI uses to construct workflows.
paragraphs.zh: 这些参数来自 Cardoen 等人的 2,595,399 个 GHA 工作流数据集 [ 10 ] 。 我们首先对该数据集进行过滤，去除了无效的工作流、有效工作流的旧版本，以及与基于 Python 的 CI 无关的工作流。 如果一个工作流符合 GHA 工作流模式 [ 42 ] ，我们就认为它是有效的；如果一个工作流所在的仓库根据 GitHub REST API [ 43 ] 显示其最受欢迎的语言是 Python，我们就认为它是基于 Python 的。 这样处理后得到了 15,285 个工作流，我们将其称为 CI Workflow Dataset 。 我们将星标数最高的 50 个工作流留作评估数据集（第四节），并使用 GitHub REST API 从其余 15,235 个工作流中提取最后一次成功的作业运行（如果存在的话）。 最终得到 7,157 次作业运行，我们将其称为 Heuristic-Tuning Dataset 。 对于下文中的工作流组件，我们提取了使用它们的作业运行的时长，剔除其中的离群值，并将其平均值作为默认阈值和乘数值。 下面我们列出这些参数值及其相关启发式规则，DynaCI 使用它们来构建工作流。

paragraphs.en: Set a timeout limit for job execution (Threshold = 319s, Multiplier = 13): In GHA, jobs. < < id > > .timeout-minutes specifies the maximum number of minutes that a job can run before it is forced to stop. It is included in the workflow if the corresponding job duration observed in the developer’s local environment exceeds 319 seconds; otherwise, it is excluded. When included, its value is set to 13 times the corresponding job duration observed in the developer’s local environment.
paragraphs.zh: 为作业执行设置超时限制（Threshold = 319s，Multiplier = 13）：在 GHA 中，jobs.< < id > > .timeout-minutes 指定作业在被强制停止前可运行的最大分钟数。 如果在开发者本地环境中观察到的相应作业时长超过 319 秒，则将其包含在工作流中；否则将其排除。 当被包含时，其值被设置为在开发者本地环境中观察到的相应作业时长的 13 倍。

paragraphs.en: Set concurrency control to prevent long-running jobs from executing simultaneously (Threshold = 138s, Multiplier = N/A): In GHA, jobs. < < id > > .concurrency prevents jobs that are in the same concurrency group from running at the same time. paragraphs.en: Set fail-fast behavior to allow all jobs in a matrix to run even if one fails (Threshold = 66s, Multiplier = N/A): In GHA, jobs. < < id > > .strategy.fail-fast , if set to true, will cancel all jobs in a configuration matrix if any job in that matrix fails. It is included in the workflow and set to ”false” if its job’s duration exceeds the threshold; otherwise, it is not included, and the value would be ”true” by default.

paragraphs.en: By the end of this phase, DynaCI is expected to result in an initial workflow file that can then be refined via LLMs.

paragraphs.en: To ensure that there are no missing components, Apply Heuristics step is designed to add components as much as possible to the workflow. However, this over-permissive design can make the initial workflow generated by DynaCI overly complicated and error-prone. To mitigate this issue, Refine with LLMs step is designed to be more restrictive. It uses an LLM to analyze runtime information, remove unnecessary and/or problematic workflow components, and patch any syntax errors that arise during refinement.
paragraphs.zh: 为了确保没有遗漏的组件，Apply Heuristics 步骤被设计为尽可能多地向工作流中添加组件。 然而，这种过于宽松的设计可能会使 DynaCI 生成的初始工作流过于复杂且容易出错。 为了缓解这一问题，Refine with LLMs 步骤被设计得更加严格。 它使用一个大语言模型来分析运行时信息，移除不必要和/或有问题的组件，并修复在优化过程中出现的任何语法错误。

sents.en: It uses an LLM to analyze runtime information, remove unnecessary and/or problematic workflow components, and patch any syntax errors that arise during refinement.
sents.zh: 它使用一个大语言模型来分析运行时信息，移除不必要和/或有问题的组件，并修复在优化过程中出现的任何语法错误。

paragraphs.en: To support this process, we extract runtime information about the GHA runner that the workflow is expected to run in, providing it to DynaCI as CI context ( Section III-D1 ). For a given initial workflow, DynaCI separates all the available runtime information into chunks and encodes the chunks into embeddings. ( Section III-D2 ). Then, DynaCI retrieves the most relevant chunks via Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) [ 17 ] to provide the LLM runtime context. DynaCI finally refines the content of the workflow with the LLM on two levels: the job-level ( Section III-D3 ) and workflow-level ( Section III-D4 ).
paragraphs.zh: 为支持这一过程，我们提取工作流预期运行的 GHA 运行器的运行时信息，并将其作为 CI 上下文提供给 DynaCI（第 III-D1 节）。 对于给定的初始工作流，DynaCI 将所有可用的运行时信息分成块，并将这些块编码为嵌入（第 III-D2 节）。 然后，DynaCI 通过检索增强生成（RAG）[17] 检索最相关的块，为 LLM 提供运行时上下文。 最后，DynaCI 在两个层次上利用 LLM 精炼工作流的内容：作业层次（第 III-D3 节）和工作流层次（第 III-D4 节）。

paragraphs.en: In every initial workflow, DynaCI sets environment variables and installs packages found in the developer’s local environment. However, in many cases, these features may already be found on a GHA runner. To minimize redundancies and potential conflicts, DynaCI provides runtime information about the target runner environment to the LLM as additional context for refinement. We acquired this information manually by running apt , pip , and env commands on the target runner.

paragraphs.en: Because each job reflects a different entry point in the developer’s local environment, DynaCI traces them separately. Thus, each job has its own runtime information. Instead of refining the entire workflow at once, DynaCI uses a divide-and-conquer approach; it extracts the jobs from the initial workflow and improves them separately ( divide ). For each job, DynaCI first retrieves runtime chunks with cosine similarity ≥ 60 % \geq 60\% of its run blocks. Next, DynaCI sends a job prompt with these chunks to an LLM with instructions to remove unneeded components from the job (e.g., environment variables, package installations) and to substitute direct references to OS and Python versions with the job’s matrix variables, which is a best practice [ 11 ] . The prompt includes information about the GHA environment that the job will run in ( Section III-D1 ) and warnings against making additional changes, as preliminary experiments showed a tendency for the LLM to hallucinate beyond the intended scope.
paragraphs.zh: 由于每个任务（job）都对应开发者本地环境中不同的入口点，DynaCI 会分别追踪它们。 因此，每个任务都有其自己的运行时信息。 DynaCI 不是一次性改进整个工作流，而是采用分而治之的方法；它从初始工作流中提取各个任务并分别加以改进（divide，即分解）。 对于每个任务，DynaCI 首先检索与其运行块（run blocks）余弦相似度 ≥ 60 % \geq 60\% 的运行时片段（chunks）。 接着，DynaCI 将包含这些片段的任务提示（prompt）发送给大语言模型（LLM），指示其移除任务中不需要的组件（例如环境变量、软件包安装），并将对操作系统和 Python 版本的直接引用替换为该任务的矩阵变量，这是一种最佳实践 [ 11 ] 。 该提示包含任务将要运行的 GHA 环境的相关信息（ Section III-D1 ），以及禁止进行额外更改的警告，因为初步实验表明大语言模型有超出预期范围进行幻觉输出的倾向。

paragraphs.en: After DynaCI receives the refined job blocks, it instructs the LLM to merge them into a single workflow ( conquer ). To mitigate hallucinations, DynaCI validates the generated workflow using actionlint , a static analyzer for GHA workflows [ 47 ] . If actionlint returns an error, DynaCI adds the error message to the workflow prompt and regenerates the refined workflow. It repeats this process until actionlint no longer produces an error, or five refinement iterations have occurred, producing the final workflow .
paragraphs.zh: 在 DynaCI 接收到细化后的作业块之后，它会指示大语言模型将其合并为单一工作流（各个击破）。 为了缓解幻觉问题，DynaCI 使用 actionlint（一种针对 GHA 工作流的静态分析器 [47]）来验证生成的工作流。 如果 actionlint 返回错误，DynaCI 会将该错误信息添加到工作流提示中，并重新生成细化后的工作流。 它会重复这一过程，直到 actionlint 不再产生错误，或已进行五轮细化迭代，从而生成最终工作流。

paragraphs.en: To evaluate the performance of DynaCI , we required a dataset that establishes a correspondence between CI workflows and their counterparts in local environments. We began with our Evaluation Dataset of 50 workflows with the highest star counts that we keep aside during Section III-C3 to ensure that there is no data leakage between our Heuristic-Tuning Dataset and the evaluation setup. For each project in our sample, we then consulted the projects’ source code and documentation to create representative local environments ( Section IV-A ). Within each environment, we generate a workflow file using DynaCI ( Section IV-B ) as well as the state-of-the-art workflow generation tools, GH-WCOM [ 15 ] and LLM4GW [ 48 ] ( Section IV-C ). We finally compare these workflows against their targets on effectiveness, efficiency, and their need for modification to answer RQ1–RQ3 ( Section IV-D ).
paragraphs.zh: 为了评估 DynaCI 的性能，我们需要一个能够在 CI 工作流与其在本地环境中的对应版本之间建立对应关系的数据集。 我们从我们的评估数据集开始，该数据集包含星标数最高的 50 个工作流，我们在第 III-C3 节中将其保留下来，以确保启发式调优数据集与评估设置之间不存在数据泄露。 对于样本中的每个项目，我们随后查阅项目的源代码和文档，以创建具有代表性的本地环境（第 IV-A 节）。 在每个环境中，我们使用 DynaCI（第 IV-B 节）以及最先进的工作流生成工具 GH-WCOM [15] 和 LLM4GW [48]（第 IV-C 节）生成工作流文件。 最后，我们将这些工作流与其目标工作流在有效性、效率以及所需的修改程度上进行比较，以回答 RQ1–RQ3（第 IV-D 节）。

paragraphs.en: Two authors manually inspected each projects’ developer-facing documentation (e.g., CONTRIBUTING.md ) and configurations (e.g., pyproject.toml ) to identify the commands that developers use to set up their local environments. For example, in httpie/cli , the CONTRIBUTING.md file mentions test-related commands, such as make test and python -m pytest . We found 90.8% of commands in our sample involve similarly generic commands, such as tox . To ensure that the reconstructed local environments were executable and representative of developer machines, we also added setup commands that were not always explicitly documented in the source code or project documentation. For instance, when needed, we installed project dependencies using commands such as pip install -r requirements.txt before executing the documented test commands. Previous works used similar approaches to identify build and test commands [ 49 ] as well as dependency installation commands [ 50 ] in documentation and configuration files.

paragraphs.en: To ensure the reproducibility of the aforementioned environments, we defined each environment in a Dockerfile that performs the following key steps. First, the Dockerfile clones the corresponding repository into the container. Second, it installs DynaCI and its dependencies (i.e., strace , ltrace , and actionlint ). Third, the Dockerfile installs the most recent Python version that the project supports as well as the package manager that the project uses, if any (e.g., uv ). Fourth, it sets any environment variables with values mentioned in the project’s source code and documentation. Lastly, the Dockerfile executes developer commands that we identified with the aforementioned approach, and which a developer would provide as an input file to DynaCI (Section III-B ).
paragraphs.zh: 为确保上述环境的可复现性，我们在 Dockerfile 中定义了每个环境，该 Dockerfile 执行以下关键步骤。 首先，Dockerfile 将对应的代码仓库克隆到容器中。 其次，它安装 DynaCI 及其依赖项（即 strace、ltrace 和 actionlint）。 第三，Dockerfile 安装该项目所支持的最新 Python 版本，以及该项目所使用的包管理器（如有，例如 uv）。 第四，它根据项目源代码和文档中提到的值设置相应的环境变量。 最后，Dockerfile 执行我们通过前述方法识别出的开发者命令，这些命令正是开发者会作为输入文件提供给 DynaCI 的内容（第 III-B 节）。

DynaCI transforms this runtime information into an initial workflow file, which then would be refined via an LLM to create the final workflow file. We treat this final workflow file as the output of DynaCI when comparing it with the baseline approaches.

paragraphs.en: To contextualize DynaCI ’s performance, we generate workflows using several (state-of-the-art) approaches:
paragraphs.zh: 为了对 DynaCI 的性能进行背景对比，我们使用多种（最先进的）方法生成工作流：

paragraphs.en: Commands-Only, i.e., using only the developer’s commands to generate a workflow: For each project, we instruct a LLM to produce a GHA workflow only using the commands that developers would be run in their Dockerized environment. This baseline evaluates whether commands alone are enough to produce an acceptable workflow with an LLM.
paragraphs.zh: 仅命令模式，即仅使用开发者的命令来生成工作流：对于每个项目，我们指示一个大语言模型（LLM）仅使用开发者在 Docker 化环境中会运行的命令来生成 GHA 工作流。 该基线用于评估仅凭命令是否足以让大语言模型生成可接受的工作流。

sents.en: Commands-Only, i.e., using only the developer’s commands to generate a workflow: For each project, we instruct a LLM to produce a GHA workflow only using the commands that developers would be run in their Dockerized environment.
sents.zh: 仅命令模式，即仅使用开发者的命令来生成工作流：对于每个项目，我们指示一个大语言模型（LLM）仅使用开发者在 Docker 化环境中会运行的命令来生成 GHA 工作流。

sents.en: This baseline evaluates whether commands alone are enough to produce an acceptable workflow with an LLM.
sents.zh: 该基线用于评估仅凭命令是否足以让大语言模型生成可接受的工作流。

paragraphs.en: Heuristics-Only, i.e., using DynaCI ’s heuristics to generate an initial workflow without refinement: Specifically, it follows DynaCI ’s Trace Commands step ( Section III-B ) and Apply Heuristics step ( Section III-C ) to produce an initial workflow, omitting the subsequent LLM-based refinement. This baseline results in more permissive workflows that can incorporate improbable components, which the refinement step might have otherwise removed. We include this approach in our paper as an ablation study to check whether the refinement step in DynaCI makes measurable improvements.
paragraphs.zh: 仅启发式（Heuristics-Only），即使用 DynaCI 的启发式方法生成初始工作流而不进行精炼：具体而言，它遵循 DynaCI 的追踪命令步骤（第 III-B 节）和应用启发式步骤（第 III-C 节）来产生初始工作流，省略了后续基于 LLM 的精炼。 这一基线会产生更宽松的工作流，可以纳入不太可能出现的组件，而这些组件本可能被精炼步骤移除。 我们在论文中纳入该方法作为消融实验，以检验 DynaCI 中的精炼步骤是否能带来可衡量的改进。

sents.en: Heuristics-Only, i.e., using DynaCI ’s heuristics to generate an initial workflow without refinement: Specifically, it follows DynaCI ’s Trace Commands step ( Section III-B ) and Apply Heuristics step ( Section III-C ) to produce an initial workflow, omitting the subsequent LLM-based refinement.

paragraphs.en: GH-WCOM [ 15 ] , i.e., a transformer-based approach that provides suggestions for auto-completing GHA workflows: GH-WCOM is trained on two tasks: (i) Next Statement (NS) , which predicts the next step in a job given the preceding workflow context, and (ii) Job Completion (JC) , which generates the remaining steps of a job given their names. Since GH-WCOM requires incomplete workflows, we remove runtime-based components, such as steps, from workflows generated by Heuristics-Only . We then treat workflow generation as an NS task, sequentially predicting each job’s next steps until the original number of steps is restored.
paragraphs.zh: GH-WCOM [15]，即一种基于 Transformer 的方法，用于为 GHA 工作流的自动补全提供建议：GH-WCOM 在两个任务上进行训练：(i) 下一条语句（NS），即在给定前置工作流上下文的情况下预测作业中的下一步骤；(ii) 作业补全（JC），即在给定作业名称的情况下生成作业的剩余步骤。 由于 GH-WCOM 需要不完整的工作流，我们从 Heuristics-Only 生成的结果中移除基于运行时的组件（例如步骤）。 然后，我们将工作流生成视为一个 NS 任务，按顺序预测每个作业的下一步骤，直到恢复原始的步骤数量。

paragraphs.en: F1 Score captures how well a given tool balances correctness and completeness in including a component in a workflow. Key-value matching metrics, such as the F1 score, are commonly used to evaluate YAML generation tasks [ 55 , 16 , 56 ] . To compute this, we first record the number of true-positive (TP), false-positive (FP), and false-negative (FN) components in each generated workflow. For example, a component is TP if it is found in both the target workflow (i.e., developer-written workflow) and the generated workflow and the values match. We then use these values to calculate the precision and recall, of which F1 score is the harmonic mean.
paragraphs.zh: F1 分数衡量某个工具在将一个组件纳入工作流时平衡正确性与完整性的能力。 键值匹配指标（例如 F1 分数）通常被用于评估 YAML 生成任务 [ 55 , 16 , 56 ] 。 为计算该指标，我们首先记录每个生成的工作流中真阳性（TP）、假阳性（FP）和假阴性（FN）组件的数量。 例如，如果一个组件同时出现在目标工作流（即开发者编写的工作流）和生成的工作流中，且其值匹配，则该组件为 TP。 然后我们使用这些数值计算精确率和召回率，F1 分数即它们的调和平均数。

paragraphs.en: The table reports TPs, FPs, and FNs to show how DynaCI ’s refinement step improves over Heuristics-Only . The Heuristics-Only approach, which corresponds to DynaCI ’s Apply Heuristics step, is more permissive: it includes as many runtime-observed components as possible, but also introduces extraneous components, increasing FPs. For example, in yt-dlp/yt-dlp , Heuristics-Only added an environment variable, NO_PROXY, from runtime information to a workflow. However, this variable prevented network traffic from routing through GHA proxy servers, resulting in an error. DynaCI mitigates this issue with its more restrictive Refine with LLMs step, which excludes as many extraneous components, such as NO_PROXY, from the Apply Heuristics step as it can. While this added step decreases FPs, it risks removing important components in the process, decreasing TPs and increasing FNs. However, DynaCI still manages to balance TPs, FPs, and FNs with these two steps, improving F1-scores overall. We used a two-sample t-test to compare F1 scores between DynaCI and the baselines; all differences in Table II are statistically significant ( p < 0.05 p<0.05 ).

sents.en: DynaCI mitigates this issue with its more restrictive Refine with LLMs step, which excludes as many extraneous components, such as NO_PROXY, from the Apply Heuristics step as it can.

sents.en: While this added step decreases FPs, it risks removing important components in the process, decreasing TPs and increasing FNs.
sents.zh: 虽然这一新增步骤减少了 FP，但它也可能在此过程中移除重要组件，从而降低 TP 并增加 FN。

sents.en: However, DynaCI still manages to balance TPs, FPs, and FNs with these two steps, improving F1-scores overall.
sents.zh: 尽管如此，DynaCI 仍通过这两个步骤在 TP、FP 和 FN 之间取得了平衡，整体上提升了 F1 分数。

paragraphs.en: Observation 2: DynaCI and Heuristics-Only generally perform better on components related to environment variables, error handling, and command execution. For example, the jobs. < < id > > .steps[*].run component runs the developer’s commands within a shell environment. GH-WCOM , LLM4GW , and Commands-Only often exclude these developer’s commands ( Section V-C ) and thus have poor F1 scores. Heuristics-Only adds apt and pip packages that the developer’s local environment accesses. DynaCI does the same but removes packages that are already installed in the GHA runner environment with an LLM. Since these package-installation statements are absent from the target workflows, they are counted as FPs, reducing both tools’ F1 scores.

paragraphs.en: Next, DynaCI and Heuristics-Only approach outperforms the others with respect to the jobs. < < id > > .strategy.fail-fast components, which stops running a job’s matrix if a single job is unsuccessful. paragraphs.en: DynaCI , Heuristic-Only , and GH-WCOM consistently outperform LLM4GW [ 13 ] and Commands-Only , with respect to components that define execution configurations, such as jobs. < < id > > .runs-on , jobs. < < id > > .strategy.matrix. , and jobs. < < id > > . steps[*].with.* . This is because, unlike other tools, LLM4GW and Commands-Only does not define or use strategy.matrix to parameterize configurations. As a result, it fails to generate multiple configuration variants or consistently propagate values to dependent components, such as runs-on and steps[*].with . Since LLM4GW and Commands-Only rely on hard-coded job configurations, they produce missing variants, inconsistencies, and FNs.

paragraphs.en: Observation 5: DynaCI ’s Refine with LLMs step removes many problematic components that its Apply Heuristics step introduces . However, there were many cases in which a package, such as a specific Python version, could not be found due to a missing package repository in the GHA environment. paragraphs.en: Observation 6: Developers must change substantially fewer LoC to repair DynaCI workflows than baseline-generated workflows. GH-WCOM and LLM4GW , i.e., our state-of-the-art baselines, require the most changes (592), with insertions dominating (340) due to two recurring issues. First, the tools almost exclusively generate commands that do not implement the functionality of their target. For example, GH-WCOM generates a workflow for pallets/flask that only installs dependencies, e.g., pip install -r requirements.txt , and does not lint the project’s source code like the target workflow. Second, they default to component configurations that are usually incompatible with their projects. For example, the approaches default to Python 3.8 (or the latest version [ 40 ] ) when setting up the CI environment, which many projects do not support.

paragraphs.en: Observation 7: Substantially fewer DynaCI -generated workflows require repairs than baseline-generated workflows. The table shows that among the 50 workflows in our Evaluation Dataset , DynaCI and Heuristics-Only workflows only require repairs in 22 and 39 cases, respectively. paragraphs.en: External Validity. Our experiments use 50 Python projects with GitHub Actions, which may limit generalizability to other languages and CI platforms. However, DynaCI can be adapted to these contexts with modest extensions because it derives workflow components from language-agnostic developer commands and their runtime behavior in local testing environments. Besides, many CI platforms have similar features [ 23 ] ; only the components’ syntax would need to be modified in DynaCI . DynaCI ’s divide-and-conquer strategy also enables future heuristics to be added for specific features in other languages. While DynaCI currently only supports Linux-based OSes, which is the most common runner in GHA [ 36 ] , in future, we hope to extend DynaCI to non-Linux environments, including Windows. Additionally, to evaluate DynaCI , we needed projects with workflows whose commands could run outside CI, and thus, our results may not fully capture CI-specific features, such as (unofficial) reusable actions. However, only 2.05% of the projects in our CI Workflow Dataset , from which our experiment projects were sampled, used such features. Our project filtering criteria further ensured that these projects have substantial complexity; thus, these commands are representative of real-world scenarios and projects.

Construct Validity. While BLEU and F1 scores capture textual similarity (RQ1), they do not fully account for the correctness of generated workflows in practice. We therefore complement them with a manual analysis of whether generated workflows require modifications to match target executions and how many modifications are needed (RQ3). Together, workflows are evaluated on a textual and a practical level, offering a more comprehensive evaluation of their performance.

Prior studies have introduced CI workflow generation tools: GHAST [ 63 ] , CIGAR [ 64 ] , PACGBI [ 65 ] , GH-WCOM [ 15 ] , LLM4GW [ 16 ] , and LLM4CI [ 48 ] . Among these tools, the closest to our study are GH-WCOM [ 15 ] and LLM4GW [ 16 ] . In fact, GH-WCOM [ 15 ] uses LLMs to complete gaps in a workflow configuration while DynaCI extends the use of LLMs to generate workflows from scratch. Then, LLM4GW [ 16 ] generates workflows from scratch, but its prompts require domain knowledge about GHA that DynaCI does not. Overall, DynaCI reduces developer effort by reusing runtime information from existing local testing environments.

Another line of research focuses on leveraging runtime information for source code generation and analysis [ 66 , 67 , 68 ] . While DynaCI also uses runtime information, it instead targets CI workflow generation, i.e., configuration synthesis. Lian et al. [ 69 ] show that LLMs are good at validating configurations, such as HBase, without specifically focusing on GHA. Those that focused on GHA, for example, Xu et al. [ 70 ] , leveraged CI/CD runtime logs to diagnose and repair failures. However, these approaches do not generate workflows from scratch. To the best of our knowledge, DynaCI is the first runtime-informed approach to CI workflow synthesis.

This paper introduces DynaCI , the first system, to the best of our knowledge, to combine runtime information with LLMs to synthesize GHA workflows. Our evaluation on 50 Python projects shows that DynaCI outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by generating more complete and precise workflows. Below, we distill the implications of our results:

Developers may use DynaCI to translate local environments into effective CI workflows with little cost and modification. Prior work shows that writing CI workflows is challenging [ 12 , 13 , 14 ] . Existing tools, such as GH-WCOM [ 15 ] and LLM4GW [ 16 ] , still require substantial domain knowledge of GHA. In contrast, DynaCI relies only on the developer’s local environment, thus reducing knowledge barriers and effort requirements. Our Observation 1 shows that DynaCI is able to produce more effective workflows than the state-of-the-art tools. Observations 6 and 7 show that DynaCI -generated workflows require fewer modifications, while Observation 4 shows that they can be produced at low cost.

Tool builders may develop recommendation systems to assist in troubleshooting problems from CI workflow generation tools, including DynaCI , which produced workflows needing the least modification. CI workflow generation tools can produce workflows that contain problems. While Observations 6 and 7 show that DynaCI workflows require substantially fewer modifications than the state-of-the-art, it can still generate problems, such as missing functionality, that developers would have to correct. Valenzuela-Toledo et al. [ 14 ] emphasize the need for tools that could troubleshoot problems in GHA workflows. Tool builders could leverage our repair categories for GHA workflows ( Section V-C ) to build a recommendation system for generated workflow repair.

Researchers may adopt DynaCI ’s divide-and-conquer approach to generate DevOps configurations beyond CI workflows. Prior work treats CI workflow generation as a single problem, producing an entire workflow at once [ 16 , 48 ] . DynaCI breaks down this problem into multiple sub-problems, each targeting an individual component in the workflow; these components are then integrated through a robust refinement process to produce a more effective an efficient workflow that solves the initial problem and requires little modification (Observation 5). Thus, DynaCI sets the foundation for a family of divide-and-conquer approaches to CI workflow generation and beyond. We encourage researchers to adopt our divide-and-conquer approach to automatically generate other types of DevOps configurations as well (e.g., Docker and Terraform).
